slides.slide_title: Introduce Greek roots: graph phone scope meter bio

content_payload.back_text: Greek roots — write, sound, see, measure, life

slides.teacher_cue: Five Greek roots that appear throughout science and academic English. graph = write: photograph, paragraph, autograph, geography, graphite. phone = sound: telephone, microphone, symphony, phonics, earphone. scope = see/examine: telescope, microscope, periscope, stethoscope. meter = measure: thermometer, centimeter, speedometer, diameter. bio = life: biology, biography, biome, antibiotic. Note: ph in these roots = /f/ (from Greek phi). Knowing these roots unlocks scientific and academic vocabulary.
slides.expected_response: Students identify Greek roots and use them to decode and infer meaning in academic vocabulary.
slides.correction_move: Show each root with its meaning. Build word webs: graph → photograph (light+write), paragraph (beside+write), autograph (self+write). Students generate more words.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students not recognising ph = /f/ in Greek root words.

slides.teacher_cue: Say photograph — photo (light) + graph (write) = write with light. ph=/f/ in both. Reveal and blend.

slides.teacher_cue: Say telephone — tele (far) + phone (sound) = far sound. ph=/f/ in phone. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say telephone orally and connect meaning before blending.

slides.observation_note: Watch for ph=/f/ in phone and long /oʊ/ in -phone.

slides.teacher_cue: Say telescope — tele (far) + scope (see) = see far. CVCe in scope. Reveal and blend.

slides.teacher_cue: Say biology — bio (life) + logy (study of) = study of life. Reveal and blend.
